patient_identity.statement: Male Individual8,7years at evaluation, maps to packet by the distinctive c.754del, severe growth/developmental phenotype and case-specific fibroblast work. Prenatal IUGR and nonambulatory/nonverbal childhood support early onset.

genotype.statement: Heterozygous NM_004500.4:c.754del, p.Asp252Thrfs*18, genomic GRCh38 g.21211454del matches source Table2 and S4; iso2 c.793del is the same reported allele. Packet VCF21211449 TC>T literally deletes21211450, whereas HGVS uses21211454.
limitations: Repeat-context left/right normalization could reconcile representations, but was not independently checked; do not claim exact VCF equivalence.
NMD escape is predicted and supported by transcript coverage, not a demonstrated50%protein decrease in this individual.

segregation.statement: Individual8 is explicitly de novo in Table2 and S4 and was assessed in a trio; no parental transmission reported for this case.
limitations: Original parental traces/raw genotypes and parentage testing not supplied. Other cohort cases include unknown inheritance and unaffected mosaic mothers; these must not be generalized to this case.

phase.statement: Single heterozygous HNRNPC variant; no within-gene compound-heterozygous phase question. De novo attribution is separate from cis/trans phasing.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors implicate de novo HNRNPC frameshift in the neurodevelopmental phenotype and show altered splicing in Individual8 fibroblasts. Source explicitly classifies the allele likely pathogenic (PS2/PM2), qualifying packet PATHOGENIC/SOLVED certainty. A second de novo CUL1 c.1942C>G p.Leu648Val remains a possible contributor.
limitations: CUL1 expression not being reduced does not exclude altered function.

Fibroblast comparison is one patient and one control; selected MAJIQ probability threshold lowered to0.5 from0.95 assuming NMD escape leaves more protein. Clustering after selecting altered patient events is not independent validation.
No allele-specific protein measurement or complete bulk-table review.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Packet captures many clinical findings but omits marked short stature, major airway/cardiac/genital abnormalities, endocrine deficiencies, hearing/vision defects and the second CUL1 candidate. Several listed negatives are merely unlisted dysmorphisms; severeID and seizure subtypes exceed source specificity.
limitations: Delayed myelination is historical and now normal in source.
Many excluded features have no direct negative assessment.

limitations: Repeat-context left/right normalization could reconcile representations, but was not independently checked; do not claim exact VCF equivalence.

Mandatory HANDOFF.md read at resume exposed aggregate benchmark outcomes and a historical HG002/FGFR2 public-control case-specific rank. Conservatively declared per_case; this old public-control exposure is distinct from target-case outcomes: no target-case inference/result files or additional outcome summaries were consulted for this review. This is post-inference source correspondence, not blinded validation. Earlier canonical reviews are inherited work and are not claimed as this reviewer reading.

All main1389lines/23pages, supplement512lines/20pages, clinicalS4 all143rows/16views, populationS5 all35rows/7views and targetS7 all77rows/8views personally read. All assigned cases/alternatives inspected. S6/S8/S9 remain unread; no complete-paper claim.
Inherited canonical records remain attributed to their original reviewers; protected parent-completed records untouched.

Individual8 possible second CUL1 contributor and unverified VCF normalization; Individual11 later6y8m growth snapshot and ambiguous fine-motor row. Both source classifications likely pathogenic, not literal pathogenic.

I1 cell results reflect one affected donor and matched control; three clones are not three independent affected people. Protein about45.15%ofcontrol but mRNA16%decrease nonsignificant (adjustedp.81). This does not directly establish all missense mechanisms.
Dose perturbation experiments in murine/cell systems support dosage sensitivity; early migration delay absent byP7. No translation to patient treatment or experimental design is made.

Figure2B star convention versus prose p.006 differs; Table1 includes inconsistent denominators/percentages (shortstature total3/12 vs subgroup2/3 with others0; seizure/hypotonia1/3 labeled50%; deepseteyes2/3 labeled100%). Narrative sleep83%vs9/12 and microcephaly4/12vs4/13 should not be silently reconciled.

AS target prose73 and workbook74rows differ. Results28same+29unchanged+3opposite totals60 rather than61; discussion52%differs from results46%. All S7entries read, but no independent recalculation from raw reads. Corrected p-values in S7 are retained as source labels without assuming a multiple-testing method.

S6C CD55 printed distributions/means repeat across4cell types; POLD3 HEK/fibroblast printed means also repeat. These displayed repetitions warrant caution and checking against underlying tables; no allegation or corrected values inferred.

S5 consequences are transcript-dependent; iso2-only predictedLoF and in-frame/splice alternatives limit blanket LoF claims. Source labels synonymous Val213Val as missense and has differing written insertion lengths across genome builds; neither silently corrected. Population counts are publication-era data, not a current gnomAD lookup.

Article nomenclature/cross-reference discrepancies include Figure6 captionc.332G>A vs Table2c.322G>A forI12, S3captionpanel lettering/S6captionDvsC, and S1C/S2Creference. Assigned I11c.296G>A remains consistent.
Raw repositories and individualized diagnostic certainty not independently reproduced. Published methods were read only to appraise evidence; no wet-lab design/execution.
